subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should the AI-only Crestodian direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100656 be the canonical fix, and if so what approval/security boundary must it preserve before merge?
rationale: The source proves real bugs, but the proposed endpoint changes CLI setup UX, rescue fallback semantics, approval intent, agent-loop state, and setup wizard security boundaries, so maintainer intent is needed before cleanup or repair automation.

options.title: Revise the AI-first fix
options.body: Keep PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100656 as the fix path, but require it to preserve approval gates, clear stale proposal state, and add real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Split the repair
options.body: Land parser and approval safety first, then track directives, executor refactor, sensitive-history redaction, and Gemini parity as separate follow-ups.

options.title: Choose a narrower compatibility fix
options.body: Anchor only the most dangerous deterministic grammar and broaden literal approvals while deferring the broader AI-only product boundary.

recommendation.title: Revise the AI-first fix
recommendation.body: Keep PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100656 as the fix path, but require it to preserve approval gates, clear stale proposal state, and add real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Crestodian feature history and candidate fix PR both point to steipete as the best available product-boundary owner.
